_note: Reported news for the PDF. Edit or regenerate weekly from the climate-news monitor. 'counties' lists every county the item names; items with no county go in scope 'national' (state or countrywide). Items older than NEWS_DAYS are dropped.

items.text: Flash flood made the Kapuri bridge overflow and briefly cut movement between Kapuri and Juba (county inferred from location).
Uganda warned of record Lake Victoria levels and higher releases into the Nile; Juba and low-lying areas flagged as vulnerable. Nile readings from Nimule to Renk are still below alert levels.
Heavy rain flooded shelters in 15 IDP camps across three payams and destroyed homes; residents report no medicines and high food prices.
40 hepatitis E cases, no deaths, in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (Aweil East, Aweil North, Gok Machar, Aweil West), linked to water contaminated during heavy rains.
Seven-day oral cholera vaccination drive with MSF and WHO targets 100,000 IDPs after thousands of cases this year.
UNMISS says heavy rain, El Nino and funding shortfalls are straining the temporary dykes kept by IOM and UNMISS at Bentiu (county inferred from Bentiu).
April-July 2026 was the second driest since 1991 (CHIRPS); a poor harvest is expected in October and food access may shrink from September if distributions end.
REACH published a rapid drought impact assessment for Lafon (findings not yet reviewed).
Lakes State restructured a peace committee citing flood fears; no damage reported (county not stated).
About 1.1 million people affected by a prolonged rainfall deficit across five counties (not named); officials fear more hunger later this year and into 2027.
National Flood Task Force activated for October-December El Nino risks; about 1.3 million people could be affected across seven states (a projection).
WFP warns over 1 million people may lose food aid by October ($86 million gap); 7.8 million struggle to find enough food.
